title: Mixed-workload scheduler canary: rollout monitoring checklist (SRE)
content:
Purpose
This is the SRE checklist for enabling the mixed-workload scheduler prototype (short/long prompt-aware dispatch) in canary and limited production slices.

Scope
- Applies to: runtime-1.19 builds with scheduler feature flag present (default OFF).
- Goal: detect regressions early (p95/p99 latency, starvation, overload/backpressure pathologies) and have a fast rollback path.
- This is intentionally “ops-first” and assumes the design/bench docs are already reviewed.

Rollout definition (fill in per event)
- Date/time window (UTC): _______________________________
- Target cluster/region: _______________________________
- Route(s)/model(s): _______________________________
- Customer tier/slice (Dedicated / Hosted / internal): _______________________________
- Flag name/config key: _______________________________
- Canary % (start -> max): ____% -> ____%
- Max duration at each step: _______________________________
- Owner on point (runtime): _______________________________
- Owner on point (SRE): _______________________________
- Comms channel: #eng-runtime + #eng-sre (and #incidents if we page)

Pre-rollout readiness (T-24h to T-1h)
1) Confirm artifact + config
- [ ] Confirm runtime image SHA / deploy version tagged for the canary.
- [ ] Confirm scheduler flag exists and is default OFF for all other slices.
- [ ] Confirm quick toggle mechanism works (no redeploy required if possible). If a restart is required, document which services/pods.
- [ ] Confirm backpressure/admission control changes are included if required for this iteration.
- [ ] Confirm canary job/report is set up to A/B compare baseline vs flag-on (perf-canary/pr_218).

2) Confirm dashboards are present and pinned (per on-call)
Pin these BEFORE we flip any traffic.
- [ ] “Mixed workload scheduler overview” dashboard (per-class queue depth + waits)
- [ ] “API latency SLO: tail breakdown” dashboard (p50/p95/p99, by route/model)
- [ ] “Runtime saturation” dashboard (GPU util, mem, batch sizes, KV cache pressure)
- [ ] “Request mix” dashboard (prompt length distribution / tokens in / tokens out)
- [ ] “Errors/timeouts” dashboard (429/5xx/timeouts, client cancels)

Dashboard panels to sanity-check (expected signals)
- Queue depth by class (short vs long)
  - Expectation after enabling: short queue depth should decrease or stabilize; long queue depth may increase slightly but must not grow without bound.
- Wait time histograms (enqueue->dequeue), by class
  - Expectation: short p95 wait decreases; long p95 wait stays bounded per fairness window.
- Service time split: prefill vs decode
  - Expectation: improvements should show up primarily as reduced wait for short + fewer short requests stuck behind prefill-heavy batches.

3) Alerts to enable / verify routing
These should be enabled for canary scope where possible (namespace/cluster filter).
- Tail latency
  - [ ] p95 latency regression alert (route/model scoped): +X% vs baseline over 10–15 min
  - [ ] p99 latency regression alert (route/model scoped): +X% vs baseline over 10–15 min
- Starvation / fairness
  - [ ] Long-queue max-wait guardrail breached (see below for rollback triggers)
  - [ ] Long queue depth monotonic increase for N minutes (slope-based)
- Overload/backpressure
  - [ ] Admission control rejects/429 elevated (short class and long class separately)
  - [ ] Timeouts elevated (especially short/interactive)
- Runtime health
  - [ ] CrashLoop / restart rate
  - [ ] Scheduler lock contention / event loop lag (if instrumented)

Note: if alerting infra can’t cleanly scope to canary slice, we run “alert dry-run” in a pinned view and rely on manual thresholds + fast rollback.

4) Staffing / on-call notes
- Minimum staffing for a flag flip:
  - SRE on-call (primary) + SRE shadow (recommended)
  - Runtime engineer who can revert flag + land hotfix if needed
- Paging policy during the window:
  - Use #eng-sre + #eng-runtime for first response.
  - Page SRE primary if any rollback trigger is met.
  - If customer impact suspected (timeouts/errors visible), move to #incidents and declare a mini-incident.
- Don’t run the first canary step during known high-risk times (major deploy trains, region maintenance, peak customer batch windows).

5) Baseline capture (required)
Capture a baseline snapshot 30–60 minutes before flipping the flag.
- [ ] p50/p95/p99 latency by route/model
- [ ] Throughput (req/s and tokens/s)
- [ ] GPU util and memory
- [ ] Queue depth/wait (should reflect baseline scheduler metrics if available; otherwise record “not available”)
- [ ] Error rates (5xx, timeouts, 429)
Save links to the pinned dashboard time ranges here:
- Baseline dashboard link(s): __________________________________________

During rollout (T0 -> end)
Rollout step template (repeat per % increase)
Step ___: canary at ____% (flag ON)
- Start time (UTC): ________
- Planned duration: ________
- Observed (attach links):
  - Latency p95/p99 (short routes): ________
  - Latency p95/p99 (long routes): ________
  - Errors/timeouts: ________
  - Queue depth (short/long): ________
  - Wait time (short/long p95): ________
  - GPU util: ________
- Notes / anomalies: _________________________________________________
- Decision: [ ] proceed [ ] hold [ ] rollback

Things to watch specifically (we’ve been burned by these)
- Priority inversion symptoms
  - Short requests show increased wait time while long prefill batches are running.
  - “Looks fine on average” but p99 spikes line up with long context bursts.
- Oscillation / burst instability
  - Queue depth swings with a period of ~fairness window.
  - Throughput dips while latency doesn’t improve (scheduler thrash).
- Misclassification
  - Sudden shift: many medium prompts labeled “short” and flood the short queue.
  - Long queue max-wait jumps even at low canary %.

Suggested manual thresholds (if alerting is noisy)
Use these when comparing the canary slice vs baseline slice.
- Short/interactive routes
  - p95 regression: > +10% sustained for 10 min => HOLD
  - p99 regression: > +15% sustained for 5–10 min => ROLLBACK unless explained by external incident
- Long prompts
  - Max wait time exceeds fairness bound (or > 2x pre-rollout median) sustained 10 min => ROLLBACK
  - Queue depth grows continuously for 15 min with no corresponding throughput increase => ROLLBACK
- Errors
  - Timeouts or 5xx: any statistically meaningful increase correlated with flag ON => ROLLBACK
- Throughput
  - Tokens/s regression > 5% sustained with no latency benefit => HOLD (don’t auto-rollback unless customer impact)

Rollback criteria (explicit)
Rollback if ANY of the following occurs and can’t be explained by unrelated infra events:
1) Short/interactive p95 increases > 10% for 10 minutes after flag ON at a given step.
2) Short/interactive p99 increases > 15% for 5–10 minutes.
3) Long queue starvation indicator trips (max-wait bound exceeded) OR long queue depth monotonic growth for 15 minutes.
4) Timeouts increase materially (especially if concentrated in short class).
5) Admission control rejects for short class increase enough to cause user-visible throttling.

Rollback steps (fast path)
Goal: return service to baseline scheduler behavior quickly and safely.
1) Disable flag
- [ ] Set scheduler flag OFF for canary scope (config/feature flag system).
- [ ] Confirm propagation completed (config refresh / control plane ack).
- [ ] Confirm new requests in canary are being served by baseline policy.

2) Traffic mitigation (if needed)
- [ ] Reduce canary % to 0% immediately.
- [ ] If canary impacted a Dedicated customer route, shift traffic to baseline pool/region if safe.
- [ ] Temporarily tighten admission control for long class if it is causing cluster-wide pressure (coordinate with runtime/SRE lead).

3) Verify recovery (must be written down)
- [ ] Short/interactive p95 returns to within 5% of baseline within 10–15 minutes.
- [ ] Queue depths stabilize (no continued backlog growth).
- [ ] Error/timeout rates return to baseline.

4) Comms
- [ ] Post summary in #eng-runtime and #eng-sre (what we saw + when we rolled back).
- [ ] If customer impact: open/attach an incident thread and link dashboard time ranges.

Post-rollout actions (same day / next business day)
- [ ] Save dashboard links for each rollout step.
- [ ] File follow-ups in Linear (classifier thresholds, fairness window tuning, metric/alert improvements).
- [ ] Update known issues page if we found a new failure mode.
- [ ] If we held (not rolled back) but saw concerning signals, schedule a review before increasing rollout scope.

Appendix A: “Dashboards to pin” quick list (copy/paste)
- Mixed workload scheduler overview
- Queue depth by class (short/long)
- Wait time histograms by class
- Tail latency breakdown by route/model (p50/p95/p99)
- Errors/timeouts (route/model)
- Admission control: rejects by class
- GPU util + memory + batch size + KV cache

Appendix B: Notes/FAQs
Q: What’s the single most important graph?
A: Short-class wait time + short p95, plotted against long prefill bursts. If short waits spike when long prefill spikes, we are not solving the problem (or we regressed).

Q: If latency improves but throughput dips slightly, do we rollback?
A: Not automatically. Hold and ask runtime/perf to confirm if the dip is within expected bounds. Rollback only if customer SLOs are at risk or queueing becomes unstable.

Q: Who can approve moving from canary to limited production?
A: Runtime on-point + SRE on-point. For Dedicated customer exposure, loop in Lauren Bishop (Dedicated PM) if there is any SLO/SLA implication.

Change log
- 2024-11-18: Initial draft (Rafael)
- 2024-12-03: Added explicit rollback triggers + starvation focus (Aisha)
- 2025-01-12: Added baseline capture requirement + throughput guidance (Sean)
